title: finding(app-shell): the generic `ConditionWidget` mount is polymorphic over metadata types whose hosts DISAGREE about which roots are bound — so it cannot take the one-line `context` declaration its two curated siblings just took
body:
The generic `ConditionWidget` mount takes the **default** subject vocabulary while being **polymorphic** over the metadata type it is editing — and that type decides whether the condition is evaluated by a **server** host (`{ record, previous }` only) or a **client** one (where `user` is bound). ⇒ one declaration at that mount would be correct for one metadata type and wrong for another.

## Why it is left standing while its two siblings were fixed

PR objectui#9949 (card objectui#9855) narrowed the two **curated** mounts, each of which has exactly one host:

- `HookDefaultInspector` 「Run only when」 → a hook `condition`. Seat-verified at source on objectstack `origin/main`, `packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts:253`–`:268`: evaluated against **two** bindings, `record` and `previous`.
- `ObjectValidationsPanel` → `rule.when` / `rule.condition`. Seat-verified at source, `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts:2713`+: `ExpressionEngine.evaluate(expr, { record, previous: previous ?? undefined })`, and an unevaluable guard **rejects the write** — the code's own words are 「rejected, not skipped」.

⛔ `ConditionWidget` has no single host. `ResourceEditPage` sets its `WidgetContext.conditionScope` from `conditionScopeForMetadataType(type)`, and `CONDITION_SCOPE_BY_METADATA_TYPE` carries **both** server-evaluated types (`hook`, `validation`) and a client-evaluated one (`action`, where `user` IS bound and removing it would take a working subject away). ⇒ the repair is ⛔ not a third copy of the same one-line declaration; it is a **per-metadata-type context derivation**, the sibling of `conditionScopeForMetadataType`.

## ⚠️ What is NOT MEASURED, and is ⛔ not a negative

Whether a **server-evaluated** condition actually reaches this generic widget today, rather than its curated inspector. `HookDefaultInspector` hides `condition` from its fallback `SchemaForm` via `CURATED_FIELDS`, but ⛔ nobody has established that **every** route to a hook goes through the curated inspector. ⇒ this card may describe a latent surface or a live one, and the first deliverable is that reading, ⛔ not the derivation.

## Class (c)

An authoring surface that offers a subject the runtime silently drops: an author picks `user.isAdmin` from the dropdown at a hook-typed mount, the expression compiles, and the evaluator never binds the root — on the validation side the write is then **rejected** rather than silently skipped, which is loud but is a refusal the author cannot predict from what they were offered.

## Dedupe words

`ConditionWidget polymorphic context subjects` · `conditionScopeForMetadataType context vocabulary` · `ResourceEditPage hook condition user subject` · `widget subject vocabulary per metadata type` · `generic condition mount default vocabulary`
